NOC is the proposed noise-orthogonal contextual estimator. EB0 is the
shared context-free baseline. RAW uses the unprojected neighborhood and
provides the matched comparison for assessing projection. RAW and NOC
each select a strength from their own context, so their comparison
includes the selector's response to the projection.

## Shared implementation

The analysis uses the stationary DaubExPhase filter numbered 4 in
`wavethresh::wd()`. For a non-dyadic input, the fixed boundary adapter
copies observations to the next power-of-two length and reflects the
result. Analysis rows fold back to original coordinates for variance
and context calculations. Synthesis retains the original sample size.
The score and noise estimate use the original observations.

The levelwise `ashr::ash()` calls use `pointmass = TRUE`,
`prior = "nullbiased"`, `nullweight = 10`, `gridmult = 64`,
`mixcompdist = "normal"`, `outputlevel = 2`, and `fixg = FALSE`.
Zero-scale masses are combined. All positive-scale components are
retained. RcppArmadillo computes the mixture update and the context bases.

The rank cutoff is $10^{-12}\max(1,s_{\max})$, where $s_{\max}$ is the
largest singular value of the local context matrix. Singular values
strictly between one tenth and ten times the cutoff trigger an ambiguity
failure. The procedure omits zero analysis rows and flags positive row
norms at or below $10^{-10}$.

RAW and NOC optimize a common strength $\omega$ over $[0,1]$. The endpoint
checks use feasible derivatives. Interior bisection requires a bracket
width at most $10^{-10}$ and normalized first-order violation at most
$10^{-8}$, with at most 80 iterations. To define the normalization, let
$u_i$ be the ratio of the endpoint marginal density difference to the
interpolated density for active coefficient $i$. With $H$ active
coefficients and $n$ original observations, the denominator is
$\max\{1,(n/H)\sum_i |u_i|+|\omega|\}$.
The code also checks native mixture convergence, posterior weight sums
and the fitted curve against an independent reconstruction.

The projection concerns fixed linear summaries under independent
Gaussian noise. The fitted priors and selected strength are learned from
the observed signal. Numerical checks certify the specified calculation.
The simulation evaluates curve estimation error on the original grid.

## Native context strengths across 100 replicates

Each row summarizes 100 selected strengths. The interval brackets the
first and third quartiles. The two rightmost columns count exact
endpoint selections. A range minimum printed as 0.000 may be positive
before rounding. EB0 fixes $\omega=0$ by definition.

| Scenario | Method | Median [Q1, Q3] | Range | At zero | At one |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C1 | NOC | 0.425 [0.338, 0.529] | [0.130, 0.807] | 0 | 0 |
| C1 | RAW | 0.583 [0.496, 0.688] | [0.364, 1.000] | 0 | 1 |
| C2 | NOC | 0.270 [0.219, 0.336] | [0.123, 0.494] | 0 | 0 |
| C2 | RAW | 0.383 [0.313, 0.442] | [0.228, 0.701] | 0 | 0 |
| C3 | NOC | 0.133 [0.115, 0.149] | [0.062, 0.252] | 0 | 0 |
| C3 | RAW | 0.208 [0.171, 0.252] | [0.083, 0.383] | 0 | 0 |
| C4 | NOC | 0.169 [0.076, 0.309] | [0.000, 1.000] | 13 | 1 |
| C4 | RAW | 0.655 [0.515, 0.831] | [0.328, 1.000] | 0 | 15 |

The simulation command writes the full records to `tuning.csv` in the
chosen output directory.
